purpose: Generated concept illustrations requested for slides 5 and 6. These are not real patient photographs or evidence of deployed AI.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create a near-square editorial photograph for slide 5 of Saathi, an Indian cancer care and family support pitch deck. Show an Indian woman around 60 in an ordinary cotton sari seated across a small light-wood desk from an Indian male doctor in his late 30s. They are having a thoughtful, calm conversation about her care, making natural eye contact. Both faces and upper bodies must be visible. The doctor listens with relaxed, anatomically correct hands. The patient looks like an ordinary real person, not a model. Place ONE smartphone prominently face-up at the center of the desk between them, tilted so the viewer can clearly see an audio recording waveform, a small microphone symbol, a pause control and an elapsed time of 02:14. This phone recording the conversation is the central storytelling detail. A modest paper notebook nearby is enough. No examination, no blood pressure equipment, no large laptop, no charts, no pills.
Camera: intimate but respectful eye-level three-quarter view, slightly elevated enough to see the phone screen, natural 35mm editorial photo, both faces and phone in focus, composition fits a square image and keeps all three subjects away from the crop edges.
Setting: believable small Indian outpatient consulting room, cream walls, muted sage and terracotta accents, daylight through a window, softly textured ordinary furniture. Warm, grounded and hopeful, not dramatic. Natural skin texture, subtle imperfect details, realistic cotton fabric, realistic fingers, honest gentle expressions. No stock-photo handshake, no posing at the camera, no glossy beauty retouching, no exaggerated smile, no futuristic holograms, no AI robot, no logos, no watermark, no caption or other text outside the tiny phone recording UI. Fictional people, not a portrayal of any real patient or doctor.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create a wide 16:9 editorial concept photograph for slide 6 of an Indian family cancer-care presentation. It must communicate one clear idea: a person can ask about their own uploaded medical records and check the answer against the original report. This is an illustration of that idea, not an app screenshot.
Scene: a realistic close view across a warm light-wood table. An Indian family caregiver in a sage cotton kurta holds a portrait tablet at a comfortable reading angle. Her older mother in a soft lavender sari sits beside her, seen naturally and only partly in the background, both calmly looking at the tablet. A doctor's hand from the other side of the table points to the matching sentence on a paper clinic visit sheet beside the tablet. The paper and tablet, not the background faces, occupy most of the frame. The paper has the simple heading "NEXT VISIT" and the readable instruction "Bring previous reports and your medicine list." highlighted in soft amber. The tablet shows a very clean cream interface, a small magnifying-glass icon and ONLY three short clear text elements: a question "What should I bring?", an answer "Previous reports and your medicine list.", and a small source label "Clinic visit note". The answer line has the same subtle amber highlight as the printed paper so their relationship is visually obvious. There are just two other loosely stacked report pages with colored tabs on the table. This is about locating an existing instruction, never diagnosing or interpreting tests.
Style: premium natural editorial photography with a restrained designed composition. Convincing Indian people, natural skin and hands, real paper texture, real device glass, candid human moment, daylight, cream, sage, lavender and warm amber accents. Balanced uncluttered framing, generously sized paper and tablet, clean readable focal points, accurate anatomy. No glossy artificial skin, no clutter, no neon, no holograms, no robot, no AI brain, no floating interface panels, no giant headline, no chart, no lab values, no brand logo or watermark. Avoid a promotional stock-photo pose. Fictional people and illustrative interface.
